subject: Where do our logs live? Non-learning commitments and retention scope
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Marco Diaz <marco.diaz@sigtech.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 17 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Where do our logs live? Non-learning commitments and retention scope

Marco — following up from our call last week. SigTech's legal team asked for a short, concrete summary of how Redwood handles customer-generated text and operational logs so we can sign off on the non-training assurance in our SOW. A few specific asks from their checklist:

1) A plain-language statement that customer text is not used to train models (and what that means operationally).
2) Retention windows for: request logs, request bodies (customer text), aggregated metrics, and scheduled snapshots/backups.
3) Where those artifacts are stored geographically for the Hosted product vs Dedicated/VPC installs.
4) Any exceptions (debug snapshots, backups retained for legal hold) and the process to request deletion/tombstone.

Can Mina/Olga confirm the precis of the statement we give customers and attach the attestation PDF? We want something SigTech can attach to procurement rather than a long technical doc.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Sales Lead, Redwood Inference

Jordan, thanks — this is exactly what we need. Our legal team attached a short vendor questionnaire (attached). Quick clarifications:

- For request bodies: we need to confirm whether any customer text could be persisted in backups or logging pipelines beyond 30 days in the hosted product.
- For Dedicated/VPC: we understand customer controls storage, but we need wording about whether Redwood ever ingests customer data into any training/experimentation environments (even internal research replicas).

If you can provide a one-paragraph attestation and a simple table of retention windows, we can move this through procurement quickly. Also confirm whether the attestation can be countersigned (DocuSign).

Best,
Marco
Marco Diaz
Head of Infrastructure & Security, SigTech
marco.diaz@sigtech.com

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Where do our logs live? Non-learning commitments and retention scope

Hi Marco — appreciate the clear asks. Below is a concise attestation and an operational retention table you can paste into procurement materials. I'm attaching a formal "No-Train Attestation" PDF for signature.

One-paragraph attestation (recommended customer-facing language):
Redwood Inference does not use customer-provided text or conversational inputs to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve any models in our hosted or dedicated offerings unless a customer explicitly opts in via a documented agreement. Operational telemetry (e.g., aggregated metrics, telemetry for performance tuning) may be retained for product improvement in anonymized, non-textual form; raw customer inputs are not incorporated into model training pipelines.

Operational retention table (Hosted API):
- Request bodies / customer text: Ephemeral in transit; persisted in short-term storage only for troubleshooting for up to 30 days by default. Explicit deletion requests are honored via our erase API and backend tombstone flow; see note on legal hold below.
- Request logs (metadata: timestamps, route, tokens processed): 90 days for audit and billing; aggregated metrics stored for up to 24 months.
- Snapshots / backups: Rolling snapshots of ephemeral worker state (for disaster recovery) are retained for a 90-day window; those snapshots are not used for model training. Longer-term archival (beyond 90 days) occurs only for legal/contractual holds and is subject to customer notification.

Dedicated / VPC installs:
- For Dedicated (Redwood-managed) instances: storage residency follows the customer-selected region; retention windows are configurable and can be set to match customer policy. Our standard commitment remains: we do not re-ingest customer text into any model training environment.
- For Private (customer-managed) deployments: the customer controls persistence; Redwood's control plane does not copy customer text out of the customer's environment for training.

Exceptions and legal hold:
- Debug snapshots or forensic copies may be created by our operations team for incident response; these are short-lived (default 30 days) unless placed on legal hold. Customers may request immediate deletion/tombstone via the erase API and the Support portal; for legal holds we will surface the scope and expected retention period.

Proof / evidence we can provide:
- SOC 2 Type II report (redacted) — available on request.
- The attached No-Train Attestation PDF (signed by Redwood security leadership on request / DocuSign ready).
- A configuration snippet showing how Dedicated customers can disable telemetry collection at the tenant level.

Notes on "we do not train on your data":
- Practically, this means customer text is never routed into our model training clusters or offline training datasets. Engineering experiments on anonymized telemetry do not contain raw customer text. Any deviation from this policy requires explicit opt-in and contractual language.

I've attached the attestation and the vendor questionnaire you sent, marked up with answers to a few items. Let me know if you want a short call to walk procurement through the wording.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Director, Privacy & Security Operations, Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0112
